'''''Afrocarpus mannii''''' is a species of [[conifer]]ous tree in the family [[Podocarpaceae]], native to the [[Afromontane]] forests of [[São Tomé Island]] in the [[Gulf of Guinea]], growing on [[Pico de São Tomé]] at altitudes of {{convert|1300|m|abbr=on}} up to the summit at {{convert|2024|m|abbr=on}}. This is the only [[gymnosperm]] found on [[São Tomé e Príncipe|São Tomé and Príncipe]]. It was formerly classified as ''Podocarpus mannii''.<ref>{{citation |author=Figueiredo Estrela |title=Diversity and endemism of angiosperms in the Gulf of Guinea islands |date=December 1994 |journal=Biodiversity and Conservation |volume=3 |issue=9 |pages=785–793 |doi=10.1007/BF00129658 |issn=1572-9710}}</ref>

It is a small tree, growing 10–15 m tall. The [[leaf|leaves]] are spirally arranged, lanceolate, 6–8 cm long on mature trees, larger, to 15 cm long and 2 cm broad, on vigorous young trees. The [[conifer cone|seed cones]] are highly modified, with a single 2 cm diameter seed with a thin fleshy coating borne on a short peduncle. The [[pollen]] cones are 1.5–2.5 cm long, solitary or in pairs on a short stem.
